The use of abdominal computed tomography in older ED patients with acute abdominal pain. Non-specific abdominal pain remains as the most common reason for acute abdomen: 26-year retrospective audit in one emergency unit. Role of surgeon-performed ultrasound on further management of patients with acute abdominal pain: a randomised controlled clinical trial. Randomized clinical trial of bedside ultrasound among patients with abdominal pain in the emergency department: impact on patient satisfaction and health care consumption. Imaging of acute abdominal pain in the third trimester of pregnancy. Laparoscopy for the management of acute lower abdominal pain in women of childbearing age.

# GRACE-2

[Home](/)   /  [Publications](/publications)   /  [GRACE](/publications/grace)   /  GRACE-2

![GRACE w tag logo](/images/default-source/logos/grace-w-tag-logo.png?sfvrsn=80a3730d_0 "GRACE w tag logo")

The SAEM GRACE program addresses the best practices for the care of the most common chief complaints that can be seen on the tracking board of any emergency department in the country, based upon research and expert consensus. These guidelines are designed with de-implementation as a guiding principle to reasonably reduce wasteful testing, provide explicit criteria to reduce foreseeable risk, and define sensible and prudent medical care.

#### [GRACE-2: Low-Risk, Recurrent Abdominal Pain in the Emergency Department](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/acem.14495)

Abdominal pain has consistently remained the most frequent chief complaint in United States emergency departments (EDs) from 2009 to 2018. The evaluation of acute abdominal pain requires substantial ED resources, including imaging, laboratory studies, nursing care, time, and patient care space. Despite the intensity of diagnostic testing, most patients presenting with abdominal pain do not receive a specific diagnosis in the ED and are discharged.

National data on ED presentations for recurrent abdominal pain are limited. Little guidance is available to emergency physicians evaluating and treating patients with recurrent and undifferentiated abdominal pain. Without guidelines for care, variance in practice could result in lower quality care, including risks of over- or under-testing, misdiagnosis, adverse effects of over- or under-treatment, higher costs, greater length of stay, and lower patient satisfaction.

The purpose of the second Guideline for Reasonable and Appropriate Care in the Emergency Department (GRACE-2) is to provide an evidence-based, patient-centric approach for clinicians in their evaluation and management of adult patients with low-risk, recurrent, undifferentiated abdominal pain in the ED.   
  
The GRACE-2 panel reached the following recommendations:

1. If a prior negative computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis (CTAP) has been performed within 12 months, there is insufficient evidence to accurately identify populations in whom repeat CTAP imaging can be safely avoided or routinely recommended.
2. If CTAP with IV contrast is negative, the panel suggests against ultrasound unless there is concern for pelvic or biliary pathology.
3. The panel suggests screening for depression and/or anxiety may be performed during the ED evaluation.
4. The panel suggests using an opioid-minimizing strategy for pain control.

##### Read the full article:  [GRACE-2: Low-Risk, Recurrent Abdominal Pain in the Emergency Department](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/acem.14495)

results.title: Guideline for the Diagnostic Pathway in Patients with Acute Abdominal Pain | Semantic Scholar
results.content: # Guideline for the Diagnostic Pathway in Patients with Acute Abdominal Pain. @article{Gans2015GuidelineFT, title={Guideline for the Diagnostic Pathway in Patients with Acute Abdominal Pain}, author={Sarah Gans and Margreet A. Developing an evidence-based guideline for the diagnostic pathway of patients with abdominal pain of non-traumatic origin and proposing the use of the following definition for acute abdominal pain: pain of nontraumatic origin with a maximum duration of 5 days. ### The Diagnostic Process for the Evaluation of Acute Abdominal Pain by Resident Trainees in Japan: A Cross-sectional Study. ### Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum and Urine S100A8/A9 and Serum Amyloid A in Probable Acute Abdominal Pain at Emergency Department. It is shown that in acute abdominal pain, serum and urine S100A8/A9 can be useful indicators of the need for surgery, but serum amyloid A had a low and nonsignificant diagnostic accuracy. ### Development and validation of risk prediction models for high-risk patients with non-traumatic acute abdominal pain: a prospective observational study. A machine learning–based model is developed to help triage nurses identify high-risk patients with non-traumatic acute abdominal pain, enhancing accuracy and safety and external validation results indicated that the logistic regression model had good extrapolation and generalization ability. D diagnostic accuracy of inexperienced readers in the evaluation of abdominal MR images for acute appendicitis improved after training with direct feedback, and the addition of DW images improved reader sensitivity. ### The role of plain radiographs in patients with acute abdominal pain at the ED. ### Laparoscopy in the Emergency Setting: A Retrospective Review of 540 Patients with Acute Abdominal Pain. ### Standard Outpatient Re-Evaluation for Patients Not Admitted to the Hospital After Emergency Department Evaluation for Acute Abdominal Pain. Standard outpatient re-evaluation is a safe and effective means of improving diagnostic accuracy and helps to adapt management for patients that are not admitted to the hospital after surgical consultation for acute abdominal pain at the emergency department. ### Imaging strategies for detection of urgent conditions in patients with acute abdominal pain: diagnostic accuracy study. Although CT is the most sensitive imaging investigation for detecting urgent conditions in patients with abdominal pain, using Ultrasonography first and CT only in those with negative or inconclusive ultrasonography results in the best sensitivity and lowers exposure to radiation.
